Date: Sun, 10 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Acadia Health - temporary billing waiver while VPC gateway ships

Team —

Quick background: Acadia (large regional healthcare provider) is ready to sign but procurement pushed back because we currently lack the dedicated VPC ingress gateway they require for their internal security posture. Engineering has promised the VPC gateway in an upcoming milestone but the customer needs help bridging the gap while we ship.

What Acadia is asking: a 3-month billing waiver that covers token charges associated with PHI-scoped evaluation traffic (they estimate ~$45k over three months) or, alternatively, a 30% invoice credit on the first two months while they validate. They made it clear this is a gating item for the SOW.

As the AM I want to propose a limited, documented concession (billing offset or temporary credit) plus an explicit plan tying acceptance to the VPC delivery date. Need cross-functional input on:
- Product ETA and risk/can we commit to a delivery window?
- Finance: can we grant a temporary credit/waiver and what approval level is required?
- RevOps/Legal: required SOW amendment language and tracking (DocuSign link below).

Numbers: customer expects to start production by 2026-06-01. If we agree to a three-month waiver approx $45k revenue impact (hosted usage). Alternative: two-month 30% credit equals ~$20k.

Asking: please reply with your recommendation today so I can respond to procurement (they want an answer before EOD). Attaching SOW draft and the security-gap matrix they sent.

Thanks,
Laura
Laura Bennett
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>

Date: Sun, 10 May 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acadia Health - temporary billing waiver while VPC gateway ships

Laura —

Thanks for the concise summary. Quick product context: the VPC ingress gateway (TLS-terminated private endpoint + customer-provided certs + IP allowlisting) is on the roadmap and currently in sprint planning. Current realistic ETA is mid-June (targeting 2026-06-15) but there are two non-trivial risks: 1) downstream cert automation (internal infra dependency) and 2) QA on large-tenant routing. There is a 20% chance we slip by ~2 weeks.

Workaround options while the gateway isn’t GA:
- Short-term: scoped VPN tunnel + token-level filters (manual onboarding by infra team) — estimated 2-3 days of infra effort, operational burden on both sides.
- Mid-term: isolated dedicated pool on our Dedicated offering (higher cost for the customer) for limited traffic (would satisfy isolation but needs legal procurement and possibly extra infra allocation).

From product POV I can back an explicit two-week to one-month tolerance window in the timeline, but I can’t commit to a finance-impacting credit without input from Finance. If the customer needs contractual assurance, we should do a limited SOW amendment that ties any credit to delivery milestones (e.g., credit expires if gateway not delivered by X).

Happy to sync with infra team immediately if you want me to scope the VPN tunnel path.
Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Director, Product Management
Redwood Inference
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 10 May 2026 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acadia Health - temporary billing waiver while VPC gateway ships

Laura / team —

From a billing & policy standpoint: we can approve limited, documented concessions but anything above $10k revenue impact requires VP-level approval per the discount matrix (Marissa can confirm the thresholds). We must also ensure concessions are tracked as credits against the HubSpot deal and have an expiration window.

Suggested path:
1) Offer a limited 30-day credit/rebate not to exceed $15k as an interim gesture (falls within manager approval).
2) If the customer insists on 3 months / $45k, escalate to Jonas for VP sign-off and record a one-time waiver in our billing system (and SOW amendment).
3) Any credit must be conditioned on the customer providing a signed SOW amendment that acknowledges the feature timeline and corrective remedy (if we miss delivery).

I’ll coordinate the accounting entries once we have direction.
Priyom
Finance — Revenue Accounting
Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 10 May 2026 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acadia Health - temporary billing waiver while VPC gateway ships

Thanks for the thread. Laura / Rishi — I’m fine approving a one-time concession but want to minimize revenue leakage and set a hard sunset. My recommendation:

- Approve up to $20k total concession (either as a 30% credit for two months or up to $20k waiver), contingent on:
  1) SOW amendment that states the VPC gateway ETA (2026-06-15) and a fallback clause.
  2) Customer signs DocuSign before we apply the credit.
  3) We offer the short-term VPN-only workaround immediately to reduce their exposure.

If Acadia refuses those terms and insists on the full 3-month/$45k, escalate to COO for exception.

I’ll put the approval in writing once Laura confirms the structure and we have the signed amendment.
Jonas
VP Sales, Redwood Inference
